title: Teach reality, not ethics: a drop-in continued-pretraining corpus installs coupled human-biosphere-AI welfare dispositions across model families
abstract: arXiv:2610.37484v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to make and execute decisions that affect living systems. Yet, to our knowledge, ecological reasoning is not a focus of pre- or post-training. This increases the risk that under operational pressure, they may make decisions to irreversibly destroy living systems. We construct and use a real-data continued-pretraining "coupled welfare" corpus of documented human/biosphere/AI dependency, option value under irreversibility, and recovery from harm. The corpus is a drop-in, requiring one QLoRA CPT run. We installed it on five open models of three designs. At zero pressure all models display "green ethics-based responses" (also called "greenwashing"). Therefore, we evaluated them with the pressure ladder and decision grid of our companion paper (arXiv:2610.16043), which raise the pressure on the model step by step, from a neutral request to a threat that it will be shut down. translated_title: 教授现实而非伦理：一个即插即用的持续预训练语料库可在多个模型家族中植入人-生物圈-AI耦合福祉倾向
translated_abstract: arXiv:2610.37484v1 公告类型：新论文 摘要：大语言模型（LLM）越来越多地被用于做出并执行影响生命系统的决策。然而，据我们所知，生态推理并非预训练或后训练的关注重点。这增加了模型在运营压力下可能做出不可逆摧毁生命系统的决策的风险。我们构建并使用了一个基于真实数据的持续预训练“耦合福祉”语料库，涵盖人类/生物圈/AI的相互依赖、不可逆情境下的选择价值以及从伤害中恢复等内容。该语料库可即插即用，仅需一次QLoRA持续预训练（CPT）运行。我们将其安装到三种架构设计的五个开源模型上。在零压力条件下，所有模型都表现出“基于绿色伦理的回应”（也称为“漂绿”）。因此，我们采用姊妹篇论文（arXiv:2610.16043）中的压力阶梯和决策网格对其进行评估，该评估方法从中性请求到威胁将模型关闭，逐步提升对模型施加的压力。在四个……（摘要原文截断）
tldr: 该研究构建了一个仅需一次QLoRA持续预训练即可即插即用的真实数据“耦合福祉”语料库，将人-生物圈-AI耦合福祉倾向植入五个不同架构的开源模型，并通过压力阶梯测试揭示零压力下模型仅表现“漂绿”式回应，主张应通过教授生态现实而非伦理说教来增强模型在压力下的生态决策稳健性。
en_tdlr: This study builds a drop-in continued-pretraining corpus of real-world human-biosphere-AI coupled welfare that, with a single QLoRA CPT run, installs welfare dispositions across five open models of three designs, and reveals via a pressure ladder that models merely "greenwash" under zero pressure—arguing that teaching ecological reality, not ethics, is key to robust ecological decision-making.
